result.markdown:
If you're talking about the original **Oz books by L. Frank Baum**, there are several that fans consider outstanding beyond the famous first book. Interestingly, the most beloved sequel isn't necessarily the one most people know.

I compared reader ratings, fan rankings, and critical commentary. Here's where I'd start.

## The best Wizard of Oz books

![1907 Ozma of Oz by L. Frank Baum — Antico](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/jWjfydfRek4jaO1FMzw1p9mGGJB97HXuTkn0z3P2kUvK1624z78jumsViOBr9Guhi7JiLYAN_0nh3KdmQ3fKQa7MGZCBEp54FCwVB8m7Lx8eX39g8D_mJ9zYhuhnzYZOxC8cXkcObUPbrgIofPfFaVxZvX3yAZ52tNfufklz9Ft2b7OmcQL1Lq3Dw9ss8DnW?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. Ozma of Oz \(1907)**

(Best overall sequel)

Goodreads: 3.95/5

Often considered one of Baum's finest. Dorothy returns to Oz, meets the magical chicken Billina, and gets caught up in a fantastic rescue adventure involving the Nome King.

---

![A Digital Archive of 1,800+ Children's Books from UCLA |  Open Culture](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/ktPSnTMEmSElZshwWTzqxNKicoMxk-5To_TV0k5UX3P4DSE6dNbSFoI-NJBmZ-0p5qSvlZbxl1y7goSG2kkLHKti8J84mByOHTqDj56vSAraePGvb9H5AAOSl-p-KS9usgOu9FI-7V3OsiPiKAocGb8oW01oeyDic5Q38s9lu2jeUdAa-ma4vNIsqKyBzaDp?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz \(1900)**

Goodreads: 4.00/5

The original and still the most highly rated. Wonderful world-building, memorable characters, and a surprisingly different experience from the 1939 movie.

---

![THE PATCHWORK GIRL OF OZ; By L. Frank Baum / Illustrated by John R. Neill by Baum, L. Frank: Good Decorated & gilt-stamped cloth (1913) | Borg Antiquarian](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/BaYzHLyGnCfdJYO9W9Wi8AZgLYYwQBedkuk6uMwLlIstJcT-m2RS2nAcVR0vJnnQQHm2WuOEdUC2He9jS0GzEwW4Lwv0oyKOw2Vr7KblRYMZR_ti9rjHnq6RZjzanwvHy332OobYc1iO0y4Jr5O7NYYUcMynUBCCznEPuA9vMmgtrtqcQ3NLq-g_eglHWvIO?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. The Patchwork Girl of Oz \(1913)**

Goodreads: 3.85/5

Particularly imaginative and whimsical. Introduces Scraps, the Patchwork Girl, one of Baum's most memorable creations.

---

![[Baum, L. Frank] Emerald City of Oz
by Baum, L. Frank |
[1910] |
Reilly & Britton |
Biblio](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/OJodjw_kD1NOGA_U9j9gI9yK2y2ncwaCQ5liv-RZr7d_IZZtdGoX0Pde9vX4JdMJOhYvFFMKeHVuo5a5wFlrirkBW4Gx2HrufX_kynQY5nH__mgQ282icALpc1-5Ki12fEW2yv6F3StYq1Q1gagyPNYTRwXefKCS-MWETvpewNW2cwl56bj3Wzs0WF-J-dc4?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. The Emerald City of Oz \(1910)**

Goodreads: 3.85/5

Excellent if you love exploring Oz itself. Dorothy's family gets to visit, and Baum spends considerable time developing the kingdom and its inhabitants.

---

![L. Frank Baum - The Scarecrow Of Oz - 1915 - FIRST EDITION | eBay](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/MZy_5bzcCgtHtDtuh4Y-0EyVVTJCKGsXvtw4I7PYxPIt-EFdGsh3Emvxdzu2mdusjMURljYpql9Xm-IRxTIGL6tbg3oRag_lu-NZ-Zk91xXEEjcmxmKardLeQkzxdqyC8drMZLP7uePmOeTHxs0_Uq2GFpEKNjVmGywqfJby6cmyYFgltPl9M3NHXmSn6Bje?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. The Scarecrow of Oz \(1915)**

A particularly strong later installment. The Scarecrow becomes involved in a struggle against a cruel ruler. Often singled out as one of the best later Oz adventures.

---

![Lot - L. Frank Baum (1856-1919) & John R. Neill (1877-1943), illus. The Lost Princess of Oz. Chicago: The Reilly & Britton, Co., 1917.](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/c7hWehMWGSxfw8A4iddyrBP187s7FrCgYnRvtNRy9YaWg8QNzSfej1uOFO4RuotvO4A1h645JYJQw7cEtBM1kh48XnPtfhQXmnnHZvUDCfkNDQokxgHd6MzsZlwIAjAsDYnPVb5j6AseM0r7aTsHXmM5crB7r-IKcls5MwpskCZnMWu9K4-Tu3qMqVNFWzt-?purpose=fullsize)

**6\. The Lost Princess of Oz \(1917)**

A mystery-adventure involving the disappearance of Princess Ozma. A great choice if you enjoy the characters and mythology of Oz.

Sources: [www.nybooks.com](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1977/10/13/on-rereading-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.goodreads.com](https://www.goodreads.com/series/41459-oz?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[marveloustales.com](https://marveloustales.com/2014/05/28/the-ozma-trilogy/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.rareozbooks.com](https://www.rareozbooks.com/oz_books_popularity.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[analepsis.org](https://analepsis.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/08/encyclopedia-of-adventure-fiction.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What the rankings tell us

There are some interesting differences\:

- **Reader favorite\:** The Wonderful Wizard of Oz, with approximately 528,000 Goodreads ratings.
- **Strongest sequel by reader ratings\:** Ozma of Oz.
- **Fan-poll favorite\:** Ozma of Oz also topped an International Wizard of Oz fan poll.
- **Critical standout among later books\:** The Scarecrow of Oz.

Gore Vidal also wrote an interesting 1977 essay revisiting Baum's Oz books, discussing how the series develops and how his own childhood favorites changed over time. [www.nybooks.com](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1977/10/13/on-rereading-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.rareozbooks.com](https://www.rareozbooks.com/oz_books_popularity.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.goodreads.com](https://www.goodreads.com/series/41459-oz?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[analepsis.org](https://analepsis.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/08/encyclopedia-of-adventure-fiction.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommendation

If you're interested in experiencing the books as fantasy literature rather than simply reading the story behind the movie, I'd prioritize\:

1. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
2. The Marvelous Land of Oz
3. Ozma of Oz
4. The Emerald City of Oz
5. The Patchwork Girl of Oz

One thing worth knowing: Baum wrote 14 original Oz novels, and the series becomes increasingly imaginative as it goes along.

**One question\:** Are you primarily interested in the original Baum books, or are you also interested in later Oz books like Gregory Maguire's *Wicked*? Those are very different literary experiences.

[www.nybooks.com](https://www.nybooks.com/articles/1977/10/13/on-rereading-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.rareozbooks.com](https://www.rareozbooks.com/oz_books_popularity.html?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.goodreads.com](https://www.goodreads.com/series/41459-oz?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[analepsis.org](https://analepsis.org/wp-content/uploads/2011/08/encyclopedia-of-adventure-fiction.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommendation

If you're interested in experiencing the books as fantasy literature rather than simply reading the story behind the movie, I'd prioritize\:

1. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz
2. The Marvelous Land of Oz
3. Ozma of Oz
4. The Emerald City of Oz
5. The Patchwork Girl of Oz

One thing worth knowing: Baum wrote 14 original Oz novels, and the series becomes increasingly imaginative as it goes along.

**One question\:** Are you primarily interested in the original Baum books, or are you also interested in later Oz books like Gregory Maguire's *Wicked*? Those are very different literary experiences.
